Pass on the fake backend (gate exit 0): evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run. The card's entry symbol thorlabs_mtd415t.mtd415t_device:MTD415TDevice was confirmed at thorlabs_mtd415t/mtd415t_device.py:28, and the inherited thorlabs_mtd415t.serial_device:SerialDevice at serial_device.py:19. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD'S HELPER: the card's decision is direct-driver while its helper field names PythonObjectDriver; this package is a direct Driver (no family-config table), as the decision says, so the property reads and the catalogue measurement action are declared explicitly. The package is deliberately read-only: it binds no temperature-setpoint, TEC-current-limit or PID/gain setter, so its only capability is cap.measure.temperature.v1 (class floor R0) and its risk is R0 for that observational capability set (MHS/spec/04-safety.md defines R0 as temperature read). The upstream setters are heating/cooling actuations (R2 or above), and the clone has no output-disable or stop request, so a heating package could not name an honest native safe state; facts.md records the write paths and why they are not bound. No Limit is declared because there is no numeric write or invoke input; site-limits.example.json was therefore not needed and the copy from the exemplar was deleted. NOT COVERED: the temperature setpoint write, the TEC current limit write, the status window and delay, critical gain and period, cycling time, the P/I/D gains, save and clear_errors. The read-only state reports the stored setpoint and current limit but never changes them. The catalogue's optional probe and location inputs are accepted and described, but the MTD415T has one temperature sensor, so they do not select a different channel. The fake is an in-memory stand-in for MTD415TDevice (the upstream has no device simulator; tests/support/mock_serial.py is only a pyserial transport stand-in) and uses only property/method names of the upstream class or its SerialDevice base; every fixed value is marked # placeholder and none is a fact or a limit. No hardware was attached; native.py was never imported or run, and reviewed_by stays null. This package is R0, so the loader's refusal of an unreviewed model-written hardware backend (R2/R3 only) does not apply and no such protection is claimed. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected for a read-only package: no actuating capability declares a limit, so SAFE-014 has nothing to probe; every other CL3 test passed.
